sentences.text:
Indore, dated : 25/01/2019:-
 Shri Ashish Gupta, learned counsel for the petitioner.
 Shri R.Joshi, learned counsel for the respondent/State.
Heard on the question of admission.
Also heard on IA No.262/2019, which is first application for suspension of sentence under Section 397 of Cr.P.C on behalf of petitioner no.2 Gulam Rasul S/o Khuda Baksh.

4. Petitioner is convicted for the offence under Section 7(i)/16(1)(a)
(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and sentenced to undergo 1 year RI and fine of Rs.5,000/- with default stipulation.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submit that during the trial petitioner was on bail.
Final hearing of the petition is likely to take time.
The petitioner has a good case in petition, hence jail sentence be suspended during pendency of the petition.
6. Per contra, learned public prosecutor has opposed the prayer.
7. I have considered the submissions of learned counsel for the parties.
8.Considering the evidence produced by the prosecution and other HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH BENCH AT INDORE (Bhole Baba Dariy Industries Ltd. And

sentences.text: Another Vs. State of MP and Another) facts and circumstances of the case, I am of the opinion that the appellant has made out a case for suspension of jail sentence.
9.9. Thus, the application (IA No.262/2019) for suspension of sentence is allowed.

1 10.10.It is directed that on deposition of fine amount and also on furnishing personal bond of Rs.30,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before this Court/Registry on 18.06.2020 and on all other subsequent dates, as may be fixed by the Registry in this behalf, the execution of substantial jail sentence imposed on the petitioner shall remain suspended, till final disposal of this petition.
11. List for final hearing in due course.
